**Observation Log:**

- [TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/05/26 (Fri) 18:26
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The study aimed to examine the relationship between openness to change, learning organization, and knowledge sharing in three private universities in Korea.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Data was collected through an online survey platform using a four-point Likert scale to measure the variables.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Analysis was conducted using polynomial regression, and the response surface was illustrated in a three-dimensional graph.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Communication played a significant moderating role in the relationship between openness to change congruence and learning organization, and between openness to change incongruence and knowledge sharing.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] High communication levels decreased learning organization and reduced the positive effects of misfit openness on knowledge sharing.
- [USER] The study examined the effects of communication between openness to change P-O fit on learning organization culture and knowledge-sharing behaviors.
- [USER] Findings explain an organizational change driver for openness to change, revealing that congruence of individual and organizational openness positively affects the learning organization.
- [USER] The study measured individual perceptions of their own and their organization’s openness to change to identify differences and similarities.
- [USER] The approach aligns with previous studies indicating that individuals’ perception is an indicator of their (un)willingness to support change.
- [USER] The P-O fit perspective should be considered for organizations to be successful in promoting organizational change.
- [USER] High-high congruence had a higher level of learning organization compared to low-low congruence.
- [USER] Knowledge sharing exceeded the midrange for both extreme levels of individual and organizational openness.
- [USER] The study revealed a negative aspect of communication in the process of universities’ organizational change.
- [USER] Previous studies presented positive effects of communication on organizational culture, performance, and effectiveness.
- [USER] Communication played a positive role in the relationship between openness to change and learning organization in this study.
- [USER] When individuals’ openness to change was less than that of the organization, they tended not to share knowledge during active communication.
- [USER] Communication can be counterproductive if unnecessary or excessive information is delivered.
- [USER] Misfit between individual and organizational openness can hinder knowledge sharing.
- [USER] Initiatives forced by an organization can discourage employees’ efforts toward knowledge sharing.
- [USER] Individuals with low openness to change are driven to share knowledge by organizational factors.
- [USER] When communication is more active, knowledge sharing is lower in cases where individuals are externally motivated.
- [USER] High levels of communication do not always result in positive organizational outcomes.
- [USER] A system related to knowledge sharing and creation in individuals-group, group-organization, and inter-organization is needed.
